chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He was asked about the limit of complaints for a sick person. So he said: 'A man may say, "I had fever today and I stayed awake last night," and he is truthful, and this is not a complaint. But the (blameworthy) complaint is that he says, "I have been afflicted with what no one else has been afflicted with," and he says, "What has struck me is what has not struck anyone else." But it is not a complaint if he says, "I stayed awake last night and had fever today," and similar to this.'

key_terms.ابْتُلِيتُ: I was afflicted/tested — ibtila' (divine testing) implies God's agency; saying 'I was tested unlike anyone' challenges divine justice
key_terms.حَدّ الشِّكَايَة: The limit/boundary of complaint — distinguishing lawful from blameworthy expression of illness
key_terms.شِكَايَة / شَكْوَى: Complaint — shikaya and shikwa are near-synonyms for complaining about illness; the Imam uses both to refine the distinction

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic limit on complaining about illness according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) draws a precise ethical distinction between permissible and blameworthy complaint during illness. Simply describing one's symptoms truthfully — such as having fever or insomnia — is not reprehensible, as it is honest reporting of one's condition. The forbidden complaint (shikaya) is one that implies uniqueness in suffering, as if God has singled the person out with unprecedented affliction, which contradicts the virtues of patience (sabr) and gratitude expected of believers in times of trial.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Salih, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the limit of the complaints of the sick person. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man is saying, ‘I have fever today and I stayed awake last night’, and he is truthful, this is not a complaint. But rather, the complaint is that he is saying, ‘I have been afflicted with what no one (else) has been afflicted with’, and he is saying, ‘What has hit me is what no one (else) has been hit with. And it is not a complaint if he is saying, ‘I stayed awake last night and have fever today’, and such as this’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Salih who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, on being asked about the limits of (negative) complaints against an illness by the patient, the Imam said that if a man says, ‘I have fever today and last night I did not sleep restfully’ and what he says is true, it is not a complaint.

A (negative) complaint is if one says, ’I have suffered like no other person has suffered and I am placed in trial as no other person is.’ Just saying that one could not sleep restfully last night and that he has fever today is not complaining against an illness.”
